title: Agents as MCP Servers — Architectural Inversion Pattern
description: New pattern where AI agents themselves can act as MCP servers, not just MCP clients. Any MCP-compatible client (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) can invoke agents by connecting to them as MCP servers. Enables agent-to-agent composition: orchestrator agents expose themselves as callable services that downstream agents can invoke via standard MCP protocol.

redundancy_check.verdict: NOVEL — existing capabilities handle agent coordination within Claude Code but cannot expose agents as externally-callable MCP servers. This pattern enables cross-tool and cross-session agent invocation via standard protocol.
redundancy_check.key_distinction: Our current agents are invoked via Task tool internally. This pattern makes agents addressable by any MCP client externally — different composition scope.

evaluation.reasoning: High capability expansion (85): cross-session and cross-tool agent invocation is genuinely novel — not achievable via current Task tool. Integration complexity is low (40): requires wrapping agents in an MCP server framework, adding ongoing maintenance. Source confidence is MEDIUM (HN secondary source). Research needed: verify whether this is a shipped pattern or a spec/proposal, find reference implementation, assess actual complexity of exposing a Claude Code agent as MCP server.
research_questions: What framework/library enables this? Is there a reference implementation on GitHub?

source_confidence: MEDIUM — HN secondary source, verify original post and any linked implementation

final_decision.reasoning: Pattern is too vague to integrate (single HN comment, no reference implementation). Workspace has no external MCP client wanting to invoke its agents — value prop is hypothetical here. The hermes agent already covers external-agent delegation. Will re-surface naturally if Anthropic ships an official spec.
